# Final Project: ARIMAX model for Electricity Consumption in Spain

```{r}
serie=window(ts(read.table("ConsumElec.dat"),start=1990,freq=12))
plot(serie, main="Gross internal consumption of electrical energy in Spain", ylab="GwH")
abline(v=1985:2020,lty=3,col=4)
serie
```

## A.1 Identification

### Plot Annual Mean(12m) vs. Variance(12m) Boxplot -> Stationarity: constant var for each level 

-> higher variance for at higher consumption level -> non-constant var: non-stationary
```{r}
m=apply(matrix(serie,nr=12),2,mean)
v=apply(matrix(serie,nr=12),2,var)
plot(m,v,xlab="Yearly Mean",ylab="Yearly Variance",main="serie")
abline(lm(v~m),col=2,lty=3,lwd=2)

boxplot(serie~floor(time(serie)))
```
Clearly, an increasing variance confirmed. Thus a log transformation applied to stabilize the variance!

```{r}
lnserie=log(serie)
plot(lnserie)

m=apply(matrix(lnserie,nr=12),2,mean)
v=apply(matrix(lnserie,nr=12),2,var)
plot(m,v,xlab="Yearly Mean",ylab="Yearly Variance",main="lnserie")
abline(lm(v~m),col=2,lty=3,lwd=2)

boxplot(lnserie~floor(time(lnserie)))
```

Then, variance seemingly constant!





### Month BoxPlot -> Yearly Seasonality
```{r}
monthplot(lnserie)

plot(decompose(lnserie))

```
Clearly seasonality is present with s=12 months. Higher consumption in winter (for heating?). Higher again in July (AC cooling).

Eliminate the seasonality applying a seasonal difference.
```{r}
d12lnserie=diff(lnserie,12)
plot(d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d12lnserie),col=2)

monthplot(d12lnserie)

```
```{r}
cat("Var for d=0:", var(d12lnserie))
```

```{r}
d1d12lnserie=diff(d12lnserie,1)
plot(d1d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d1d12lnserie),col=2)

cat("Var for d=1:", var(d1d12lnserie))

# 2nd regular difference
d1d1d12lnserie=diff(d1d12lnserie,1)
plot(d1d1d12lnserie)
abline(h=0)
abline(h=mean(d1d1d12lnserie),col=2)
cat("\nVar for d=2:", var(d1d1d12lnserie))
```
--> One regular difference is sufficient. For d=2 the var increases again --> overdifferencing


```{r}
acf(d1d12lnserie, ylim=c(-1,1),col=c(2,rep(1,11)), lwd=2, lag.max=72)
pacf(d1d12lnserie, ylim=c(-1,1),col=c(rep(1,11),2), lwd=2, lag.max=72)
```
P=1, 2, 3
p = 1-5

MA(1) because ACF shows 1 significant lag and then not
PACF shows few small spikes, with no clear decay pattern → no strong AR structure.

ARIMA(0,1,1) ← (no AR, MA(1))
ARIMA(1,1,1) ← (weak AR(1), MA(1))

ACF:
Spike at lag 12 (not shown clearly in cropped plot but often visible if seasonal) → implies Q = 1

P=0 or 1

--> not more due to sparsity

SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]	MA(1) + seasonal MA(1) — common baseline
SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]	Adds AR(1)
SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1)[12]	Full general model
SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,1,0)[12]	MA(1) + seasonal AR(1)



```{r}
(mod1=arima(d1d12lnserie,order=c(0,1,1),seasonal=list(order=c(0,1,1),period=12)))

(data.frame("Estimate" = mod1$coef,"Lower Bound" = mod1$coef- 1.96 * diag(sqrt(mod1$var.coef)),"Upper Bound" = mod1$coef + 1.96 * diag(sqrt(mod1$var.coef))))

```

We use the CLT to assume that the estimates are asymptotically normal distributed and check if the 95% confidence interval of the estimates overlaps with 0.

We see that the coefficient estimate for theta1 and Theta the 95% confidence interval does not overlap with 0. Thus we follow that the statement that these two coefficients are significant. The intercept is not statistically significant from 0, but with 95% confidence so small that we can neglect it and assume the intercept 0.


```{r}
# Define the models to test
model_specs <- list(
  "SARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]" = list(order = c(0,1,1), seasonal = c(0,1,1)),
  "SARIMA(0,1,2)(0,1,2)[12]" = list(order = c(0,1,2), seasonal = c(0,1,2)),
  "SARIMA(1,1,2)(1,1,2)[12]" = list(order = c(1,1,2), seasonal = c(1,1,2)),
    "SARIMA(1,1,3)(1,1,3)[12]" = list(order = c(1,1,3), seasonal = c(1,1,3)),

  "SARIMA(1,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]" = list(order = c(1,1,1), seasonal = c(0,1,1)),
  "SARIMA(1,1,0)(1,1,0)[12]" = list(order = c(1,1,0), seasonal = c(1,1,0)),
  "SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,1,1)[12]" = list(order = c(1,1,1), seasonal = c(1,1,1)),
  "SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,1,0)[12]" = list(order = c(0,1,1), seasonal = c(1,1,0))
)

# Create an empty results list
results <- list()

# Loop through each model and fit
for (model_name in names(model_specs)) {
  spec <- model_specs[[model_name]]
  fit <- arima(
    d1d12lnserie,
    order = spec$order,
    seasonal = list(order = spec$seasonal, period = 12)
  )

  # Extract coefficient table with confidence intervals
  se <- sqrt(diag(fit$var.coef))
  coefs <- fit$coef
  lower <- coefs - 1.96 * se
  upper <- coefs + 1.96 * se
  signif <- !(lower <= 0 & upper >= 0)

  # Add to results list
  results[[model_name]] <- list(
    Coefs = coefs,
    Significant = signif,
    AIC = fit$aic,
    BIC = AIC(fit, k = log(length(d1d12lnserie))),
    LogLik = as.numeric(logLik(fit)),
    Sigma2 = fit$sigma2
  )
}

# Combine into a single data frame
library(dplyr)

summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(name) {
  res <- results[[name]]
  data.frame(
    Model = name,
    AIC = res$AIC,
    BIC = res$BIC,
    LogLik = res$LogLik,
    Sigma2 = res$Sigma2,
    Coefs = paste(names(res$Coefs), round(res$Coefs, 3), sep = "=", collapse = "; "),
    Significant = paste(names(res$Significant)[res$Significant], collapse = ", ")
  )
}), .id = NULL)

# Print the summary table
print(summary_table)
```


```{r}
ultim=c(2018,12)
mod1_pdq=c(2,1,1)
mod1_PDQ=c(0,1,1)

mod2_pdq=c(1,1,2)

(mod1_A=arima(lnserie1,order=mod1_pdq,seasonal=list(order=mod1_PDQ,period=12)))
(mod1_B=arima(lnserie2,order=mod1_pdq,seasonal=list(order=mod1_PDQ,period=12)))

(mod2_A=arima(lnserie1,order=mod2_pdq,seasonal=list(order=mod2_PDQ,period=12)))
(mod2_B=arima(lnserie2,order=mod2_pdq,seasonal=list(order=mod2_PDQ,period=12)))

```
```{r}
mod1_pred=predict(mod1_B,n.ahead=12)
mod1_pr<-ts(c(tail(lnserie2,1),mod1_pred$pred),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod1_se<-ts(c(0,mod1_pred$se),start=ultim,freq=12)

mod2_pred=predict(mod2_B,n.ahead=12)
mod2_pr<-ts(c(tail(lnserie2,1),mod2_pred$pred),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod2_se<-ts(c(0,mod2_pred$se),start=ultim,freq=12)

#Intervals
mod1_tl<-ts(exp(mod1_pr-1.96*mod1_se),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod1_tu<-ts(exp(mod1_pr+1.96*mod1_se),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod1_pr<-ts(exp(mod1_pr),start=ultim,freq=12)

mod2_tl<-ts(exp(mod2_pr-1.96*mod2_se),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod2_tu<-ts(exp(mod2_pr+1.96*mod2_se),start=ultim,freq=12)
mod2_pr<-ts(exp(mod2_pr),start=ultim,freq=12)


ts.plot(serie,mod1_tl,mod1_tu,mod1_pr,lty=c(1,2,2,1),col=c(1,4,4,2),xlim=c(2014,2020),type="o",main=paste("Model ARIMA(",paste(mod1_pdq,collapse=","),")(",paste(mod1_PDQ,collapse=","),")12",sep=""))
abline(v=2014:2020,lty=3,col=4)

ts.plot(serie,mod2_tl,mod2_tu,mod2_pr,lty=c(1,2,2,1),col=c(1,4,4,2),xlim=c(2014,2020),type="o",main=paste("Model ARIMA(",paste(mod2_pdq,collapse=","),")(",paste(mod2_PDQ,collapse=","),")12",sep=""))
abline(v=2014:2020,lty=3,col=4)
```

```{r}
source("CalendarEffects.r")
data=c(start(serie)[1],start(serie)[2], length(serie)) #starting year, month, series size
length(serie)

(wTradDays=Wtrad(data)) #creates auxiliary variable for trading days configurations (5/2 the ideal proportion)
(wEast=Weaster(data)) #creates auxiliary variable for Easter configurations (half easter on March and other half on April: ideal distribution)


#(mod1EC = arima(
 #       d12lnserie,
  #      order=c(2,1,1),
   #     seasonal = list(order=c(0,1,1), period = 12),#D=0 as we use d12lnserie
    #    include.mean = TRUE, xreg=data.frame(wTradDays,wEast)))
(mod1EC=arima(serie,order=c(2,1,1),seasonal=list(order=c(0,1,1),period=12),xreg=data.frame(wTradDays,wEast)))

(mod2EC=arima(serie,order=c(1,1,2),seasonal=list(order=c(0,1,1),period=12),xreg=data.frame(wTradDays,wEast)))


mod1_EfecTD=coef(mod1EC)["wTradDays"]*wTradDays
mod1_EfecIN=coef(mod1EC)["wEast"]*wEast

mod2_EfecIN=coef(mod2EC)["wEast"]*wEast
mod2_serieEC=serie-mod2_EfecTD-mod2_EfecIN
plot(mod2_EfecTD+mod2_EfecIN)

plot(serie)
lines(mod1_serieEC,col=2)
lines(mod2_serieEC,col=2)
abline(v=1992:2020,lty=3,col=4)

d1d12mod1_serieEC=diff(diff(mod1_serieEC,12))
d1d12mod2_serieEC=diff(diff(mod2_serieEC,12))


```
```{r}
source("atipics2.r")

mod1EC.atip=outdetec(mod1EC,dif=c(1,12),crit=2.8,LS=T) # automatic detection of outliers with crit=2.8 and LS =TRUE
mod2EC.atip=outdetec(mod2EC,dif=c(1,12),crit=2.8,LS=T)

#Estimated residual variance after outliers detection and treatment
mod1EC.atip$sigma
mod2EC.atip$sigma


atipics=mod.atip$atip[order(mod.atip$atip[,1]),]
meses=c("Ene","Feb","Mar","Abr","May","Jun","Jul","Ago","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dic")

data.frame(atipics,Fecha=paste(meses[(atipics[,1]-1)%%12+1],start(lnserie)[1]+((atipics[,1]-1)%/%12)),perc.Obs=exp(atipics[,3])*100)
```

```{r}
ultim=c(2018,12)


serie.lin1=window(serie.lin,end=ultim+c(1,0))

```

```{r}
pred=predict(modEC.lin2,n.ahead=12,newxreg=window(cbind(wTradDays,wEast),start=c(ultim[1]+1,1)))
predic=pred$pr
wLS=sum(modEC.atip$atip[modEC.atip$atip$type_detected=="LS" & modEC.atip$atip$Obs<=length(serie)-12,3])
pr<-ts(c(tail(serie2,1),predic+wLS),start=ultim,freq=12)


se<-ts(c(0,pred$se),start=ultim,freq=12)

#Intervals
tl<-ts(pr-1.96*se,start=ultim,freq=12)
tu<-ts(pr+1.96*se,start=ultim,freq=12)
pr<-ts(pr,start=ultim,freq=12)

ts.plot(serie,tl,tu,pr,lty=c(1,2,2,1),col=c(1,4,4,2),xlim=ultim[1]+c(-3,2),type="o",main="Model ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)12+TD+IC+Outliers")
abline(v=(ultim[1]-3):(ultim[1]+2),lty=3,col=4)
```
